issue_plan.name: Run merged-plan decision follow-ups
issue_plan.summary: First amend the follow-up core's effect outcomes, the issue protocol and recovery rules so they support real decision follow-ups without weakening ordinary builds. Then add tested decision adapters, durable execution through Workflow and watcher integration that records a merged plan's owed decision in one pull request, repairs it within its allowance and merges it on current CI. The rollout updates SPEC.md, README.md and agent instructions to replace manual decision recording with the factory's follow-up. Whoever merges records these changes' decisions, including the modeled amendments and final rollout; no plumbing build writes decisions/.

issues.title: Model recoverable decision follow-up effect outcomes
issues.body:
Project: factory/decision-followup

Before #421 wires #417/#420's Workflow, amend its boundary with real effects. Repair spends an allowance and enters Open/CIPending with no failed-repair outcome; AutoMerge enters terminal Merged before GitHub can refuse. After passing CI, a head change cannot invalidate that result because CheckCompletes accepts only pending CI. Plumbing cannot repair these gaps by resetting snapshots or inventing observations.

Model recoverable repair and merge authorization/outcomes, revision/CI invalidation and external merge observation. Preserve #417's policy: only an owed merged plan starts work; evidence determines decided-by-agent versus proposed; one stable follow-up stays in its allowed scope; failed drafts/creation retry automatically; at most two repairs occur per allowance; only an explicit authorized retry/resume renews it; closure and exhaustion wait for a person.

Charge each authorized repair attempt exactly once, including an agent that fails or leaves no publishable change. Such an outcome retains the real failure/conflict cause and can exhaust the allowance; it must neither fabricate a GitHub CI failure nor wait forever for a run that was never requested. Published repairs require fresh CI. Report repair execution failure separately from CI, and keep interrupted effects recoverable without running an attempt twice.

An accepted merge authorization is not a completed remote merge. Reconcile success or a lost response; on a definitive refusal return to a truthful nonterminal condition reflecting the observed head, CI, conflict or closure. New revisions invalidate prior CI without changing repair usage or lifting a hold. Closure during an in-flight effect remains effective; a person must explicitly resume that same PR. Record an externally merged PR as externally settled without pretending the factory merged it or supplying invented passing CI. Stable operation identities and outcome guards must reject stale completions.

Amend the model, proved core, explorer and project README through ratification and run the full gate. Add witnesses and counterexamples for failed/no-change repairs, exhaustion and renewal, head movement after CI, closure/conflict after merge authorization, lost replies, external merge and stale outcomes. Preserve the existing classification, scope and artifact guarantees. Later protocol/recovery work composes these operations; the adapters remain tested plumbing.

Basis: #417's ratified statements, #421's persisted-snapshot and real-effect requirements, D-0064/D-0069 and D-0122. The merger records this amendment's decision. Do not claim the watcher uses it yet.

issues.title: Authorize decision follow-ups in the issue protocol
issues.body:
Project: factory/protocol

After the follow-up effect-outcome amendment, authorize its integration in factory/protocol. D-0064 requires every issue step to follow this core. The current protocol ends at the merged source issue and allows factory merges only for its ordinary proposal, ratified lock and one-project scope. A decision follow-up needs distinct authority.

Amend the ratified protocol to authorize a linked decision-follow-up work item whose authority is the exact ratified plan, its merged pull request and its owed decision. Keep the source plan's merged history and ratification intact. The follow-up has its own stable pull-request identity, current head, CI and scope. It requires the corresponding accepted step of the amended factory/decision-followup.Workflow. Its classification, retries, two repairs per allowance, holds and effect outcomes remain that core's policy. Only an authenticated person with repository write access can request retry or resume, never a bot. Closing the follow-up preserves its human hold. A retry of blocked work renews its allowance; a retry of closed work explicitly resumes the same pull request. Neither restarts or replaces the already merged source build.

Define the narrow follow-up artifact class: only decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md, tied to its source obligation, with no new plan ratification or fabricated project lock. Its current CI includes the decision graph check. Existing docs/decisions CI may intentionally skip the full project gate; that is admissible only together with successful current-revision decision checks and independently verified follow-up scope. Ordinary build scope, current-head CI, lock ratification, trusted-base merge restrictions and command authorization retain their existing meaning. An unrelated PR cannot acquire follow-up authority merely by a branch name or a claimed source.

Prove the amended core, update its explorer, pinned statements through the normal ratification flow and project README, and run the project's complete verification gate. Include witnesses for an eligible human-merged plan leading to a follow-up merge, a closed follow-up resuming under the same identity, and continued ordinary build behavior. Include counterexamples for an unmerged or non-owing source, a forged association, broader scope, stale CI/head and an unauthorized retry. This issue changes the modeled authorization boundary, not the watcher adapters. Keep ordinary operations usable by the existing watcher until later plumbing enables follow-ups.

Basis: D-0064, D-0105/D-0109 and D-0079/D-0080; #417's ratified authority, scope, identity and current-CI rules and the preceding effect-outcome amendment. The merger records this amendment's decision and keeps root docs accurate under D-0122 without claiming live watcher integration.

issues.title: Recover decision follow-ups across crashes and watchers
issues.body:
Project: factory/recovery

After the follow-up and protocol amendments, extend recovery to authorize their effects for #421. D-0069 requires this core's permission. It currently knows ordinary Solve/Build runs, replacement builds and watched drafts, not automatic follow-up attempts, same-PR repair pushes or reopening.

Amend recovery for a follow-up identified by its source ratified-plan obligation and a stable branch/PR identity. Distinguish each recorded draft, creation and repair operation from that stable identity. Failed drafting and creation may start a fresh recorded attempt automatically under Workflow; a stopped or completed operation is never unknowingly run twice. Repairs publish new contents to the same PR, invalidate prior CI and consume exactly the allowance authorized by Workflow. A writer's explicit retry/resume is consumed once, renews the allowance to two and, for closed work, permits reopening the same PR. Closure or exhausted repairs remains a hold until such a request. Existing ordinary retry/replacement behavior stays intact.

Represent durable accepted Workflow snapshots and pending/completed effect identities so every accepted snapshot is kept before subsequent work is dispatched. Record agent attempts and publication/merge intent before their effects; reconcile durable results and GitHub observations after crashes or lost responses. Persist accepted merge authorization before dispatch and promote its result only through the amended core's outcome handling. After restart, reconcile success, an unknown response or a definitive refusal; authorization alone never proves a remote merge. Losing a PR-creation response must adopt the already created PR, including when a person has since closed or merged it, rather than creating another. A repair push with a lost response must not spend a second repair. An externally merged PR settles through the amended observation path without fabricated CI or another merge dispatch. Failed/no-change repairs and revision invalidation follow the amended core, retaining their attempt usage and real failure cause.

Preserve lease fencing, at-most-once operation starts, one PR for the source obligation across all attempts and holds, one merge, command-answer deduplication and rejection of stale results from older operations or watchers. Reopening is its own authorized effect; do not reuse replacement's close-and-new-PR transition. Current-head CI and mergeability observations must belong to the revision being acted on. Include progress under the existing fairness assumptions, with human holds respected.

Update the model, proved core, explorer and project README through ratification and run the complete verification gate. Witness automatic draft/create recovery, repair after CI failure, exhaustion then explicit renewal, closed-PR resumption, lost publication/merge responses, and two watchers with crashes. Counterexamples must expose duplicate creation/run/merge, a stale repair result, an unrecorded effect, lease loss, reused CI and resumption without a person. This issue adds recovery rules; later plumbing maps real records and effects onto them.

Basis: D-0069/D-0074, D-0203/D-0210/D-0212/D-0225, #417 and the preceding follow-up/protocol amendments. Preserve their run, identity, allowance and hold guarantees. The merger records this amendment and any root documentation correction required by D-0122.

issues.title: Draft and validate decision follow-up changes
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

After #421's modeled prerequisites, build the tested artifact and agent adapters and add the root dependency/replace for the local factory/decision-followup module. Workflow delegates decision text, classification inputs and artifact validation to these adapters. Watcher dispatch follows in the remaining issues.

Give the adapter immutable evidence: the exact ratified plan and its hash, the actual merged change and source commit identities, and its final persisted factory review (BuildResult.Review). The obligation must come from the ratified plan, not editable issue or PR text. Define a stable, persistable obligation representation that supports existing plans whose Summary says a decision is owed; preserve their existing hashes and records. Any new obligation metadata participates in new ratifications without changing old hashes. An already recorded discharge must not create another debt, and uncertain evidence must be reported rather than fabricated. The adapter exposes the result to the coordinator; it does not start a historical backfill itself.

An agent drafts the decision's text, door, executed/needs-owner classification inputs, provenance and, for a one-way door, options, reasoning and what would reopen it. Use Workflow.DraftSucceeds to determine the accepted classification: an executed two-way door inferred from the evidence to need no owner input is decided by agent; one-way, unexecuted and owner-input cases remain proposed. Never ratify as a person. Persist the chosen agent and its working context so later repairs use that same agent and candidate, including after reconstruction. Support the factory's configured agent backends with the same isolation and regular-file handling as other factory runs; agents receive no GitHub credentials and do not push, post or merge.

Creating the bundle actually runs invariant decisions decide with the accepted classification, captures its decision ID and generated journal/log, and supplies the one-way full record when required. The CLI's -record option only records a slug, so the adapter must also produce the full record. Persist the command result and candidate journal before publication, and reconcile them on retried creation to reuse the same published decision. A crash before an unpublished local result can be recovered may leave an unused reserved ID; this does not authorize publishing a second decision for the obligation. Do not assume that a local SQLite write and a remote record are one atomic operation. Run the command with an isolated factory-owned checkout/store. Use the command for decision writes and generated log updates; never hand-edit journal lines or the log table.

Cite the new decision on every surviving SPEC line and README passage written by the actual merged diff, including multiline text, and roll SPEC up to describe the implemented change. Preserve later unrelated documentation changes when preparing against the current base, and report ambiguous mappings instead of dropping coverage. Validate that the journal, log, record, citations and classification agree and that decisions check passes against the relevant base. Accept only regular files within decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md. Repairs receive the CI/conflict findings in the same agent context, preserve the decision's identity and accepted classification, and obey that same scope.

Acceptance tests must exercise real local decide execution without a live agent or network, journal/log agreement, two-way decided/by-agent and one-way proposed/full-record cases, owner-input/unexecuted proposed cases, complete citations and SPEC roll-up, legacy plan/hash compatibility, and reuse after a creation interruption. Test agent-context recovery, later doc edits, missing citations, invalid artifacts and attempts to return links or out-of-scope files. Keep ordinary plumbing's inability to write decisions/ intact. Update any affected SPEC/README description in this change to describe only the available adapters, not a live watcher.

Basis: #417/#420 and its outcome amendment; D-0096/D-0097, D-0105, D-0122 and D-0133. The merger records the implementation decision. No decisions/ file is part of this plumbing build's writable scope; generated bundles are test/runtime outputs.

issues.title: Persist and execute decision follow-ups through the proved cores
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

After #421's modeled prerequisites and bundle adapters, implement the durable coordinator and real repository/GitHub adapters using the installed local follow-up module. Given an eligible merged plan, drive Workflow with a repair limit of two and shared durable evidence/snapshots. Live watch wiring follows in the next issue.

Key work by the source ratified-plan obligation, preserving its plan hash, merged source revision, review, draft, decision ID, agent context, branch, PR identity, current revision and consumed human commands across polls and restarts. Accept only steps admitted by Workflow and the amended issue/recovery cores. Persist accepted snapshots atomically before subsequent work, with the pending/completed effect records needed to recover after any dispatch boundary. Reconcile saved runs, branches and all-state PR lookup before repeating effects. A restart after decision creation, PR creation, repair push, reopen or merge must adopt the existing result; it must not publish a second decision or create a second PR, consume another repair or lose an outstanding terminal merge. Use the amended core to record external settlement, failed/no-change repairs, revision invalidation and definitive merge refusals; never force a snapshot or fabricate CI. Existing lease and tenure checks cover every new effect.

Add the GitHub operations needed for reopening and reading current CI/conflict information, with lease wrappers and fault-injectable interfaces. Read and validate the checks' workflow/run identity as well as head and conclusion; the existing name-only CheckRun fields are insufficient to authenticate the gate workflow and correlate its checks. A failed draft/create attempt is retried automatically under the core. Failed CI or a merge conflict gets at most two repairs of the same PR by the same agent, each invalidating previous checks and requiring fresh results. Exhaustion blocks; one authenticated retry gives two more repairs. A person closing the PR leaves it closed across polls and restarts; an explicit resume reopens that PR with a fresh allowance. Errors, missing evidence or an unfinished repair must never be converted into a passing result.

Use a reserved follow-up branch namespace outside ordinary invariant/ build branches, such as invariant-decisions/, so the existing docs/decisions CI path can check a bundle without a fabricated project or changed plan lock. No .github/ change is needed. This is a narrowly authorized artifact class: trusted code validates the source's merged ratified plan and owed obligation, stable follow-up identity and exact current-head diff before publication and again before merge. Allow only decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md; a matching branch name or agent-supplied receipt alone grants no authority. Keep ordinary scope/ratification and trusted-base checks unchanged.

For this class, CI passes only with the repository gate workflow's completed successful What changed check, which runs decisions check, for the current follow-up revision, plus invariant/gate success or its intentional docs-only skip. Admit that skip only for independently validated follow-up scope and a successful decision check from the same current run/revision; missing, stale, queued, canceled, failed or unreadable checks never pass. An unknown mergeability result waits. Read the head and conflict status again immediately before merge and send the expected SHA to GitHub. Merge only when Workflow and recovery authorize it; record its observed outcome through the amended core. A refusal after persisted authorization must still respect a changed head, new conflict or human closure.

Acceptance tests use fake agents/GitHub and real temporary repositories: a two-way bundle merges once, a one-way bundle remains proposed, stale checks and head changes prevent merge, a conflict repairs, the third failing CI blocks after two repairs, and retry allows exactly two additional repairs. Close after zero, one or two repairs, restart, and explicitly resume the same PR. Inject crashes/lost replies at snapshot, run, command, push, create, repair, reopen and merge boundaries and exercise two watchers/lease loss and an externally merged PR. Test failed/no-change repairs, refusal after merge authorization, revision invalidation, missing/failed checks beside a skipped gate, same-named checks from another workflow, mixed-run evidence, wrong source/hash, forged association and out-of-scope files. Document the new artifact and CI contract without claiming automatic discovery is active.

Basis: #417/#420 and the preceding modeled amendments; D-0064/D-0069, D-0079/D-0080, D-0096, D-0105/D-0109, D-0122/D-0133 and D-0237. The merger records the coordinator and artifact/CI decisions; this build does not edit decisions/.

issues.title: Run decision follow-ups from the watcher
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish #421 by wiring the merged-plan decision coordinator and its real adapters into invariant watch. The prior issues have supplied ratified protocol/recovery support, agent-generated decision bundles and durable execution. This change activates them and removes manual decision recording from the ordinary merger/reviewer workflow.

When a plan's PR merges and its ratified plan says a decision remains owed, register and drive its one follow-up. In particular, observe a person's merge of a trusted-base plan even when GitHub closes the source issue before the next poll, or the watcher restarts between the merge and registration. Discover source merges from durable source-plan/build records and GitHub, rather than only OpenIssues; persist a repository-shared activation/discovery frontier and pending obligations so closing the source issue does not strand a follow-up. Paginate the source history and include merges during watcher downtime; another watcher resumes the same frontier rather than starting a new local watermark. Preserve the source plan's final merged state and existing parent plan-of-issues completion behavior. Plans not merged, owing no decision or already discharged start no decision work. Handle existing prose obligations without rewriting old ratified records, and deduplicate against recorded discharges. This rollout handles merges observed from its activation onward and all already registered work; it does not automatically backfill unrelated historical plans.

Supply the actual merged diff, exact ratified plan and final stored review to the adapter. Configure the selected agent and restore its saved context for repairs. Wire the real command, GitHub, storage and lease adapters through the CLI. Only factory code publishes and merges. Poll current CI/conflicts and execute the core's draft/create retry, two-repair allowance, block and merge behavior. Repeated polls, restarts and new watchers continue the same obligation and PR.

Route a writer's /invariant retry on the follow-up PR, or its source issue while it has that outstanding follow-up, to Workflow.Retry for blocked work or Workflow.Resume for closed work. Bind each command once to the intended follow-up and its hold, retain permission checks excluding bots/non-writers, and do not invoke the source build's replacement retry. Closing the follow-up maps to Workflow.Close and leaves it closed until an explicit resume. Posts identify the source plan and follow-up, the CI/conflict or hold, remaining repair allowance and what retry will do; after merging they identify the recorded decision and follow-up PR. Commands received before the hold they would release must not silently authorize a later hold.

In this same activation change, update SPEC.md, README.md, applicable AGENTS.md guidance, planner/build/review prompts and merger-facing text. They must say that the factory records an eligible merged plan's decision through this follow-up, with decided-by-agent versus proposed classification, limited scope, its current CI contract, two repairs, explicit renewal and closure/resumption. Plans still declare a decision owed, and ordinary plumbing builds still cannot write decisions/. Reviewers and merger checklists stop assigning decision recording as Merger work; unavailable Docker/network checks retain their existing treatment, and opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain CI's responsibility. Update existing tests that assert the superseded wording. New/changed SPEC bullets cite recorded decisions supporting them, including the prerequisite decisions once merged, as decisions check requires. The merger records the rollout decision itself, as #421 requests, without waiting for this newly installed watcher to record its own authorization.

End-to-end Go acceptance tests must drive the real watcher dispatch with controlled agents/GitHub: a human-merged two-way plan creates exactly one decided/by-agent follow-up and merges on current passing CI; a one-way plan records proposed; repeated failed CI repairs at most twice, waits, and a writer's retry grants exactly two more. Also cover a source issue closed by merge before polling, restart before registration and during an outstanding follow-up, downtime with more than one page of source merges, no debt/already discharged sources, legacy summaries, PR closure then same-PR resume, unauthorized/replayed/early retry, stable agent use, and preservation of ordinary plan/build/parent completion behavior. Verify the prompt and documentation change and run relevant existing factory/CLI/agent tests. Tests use no live watch, paid agent or GitHub mutation.

Basis: #421, #417/#420 and the preceding prerequisite decisions; D-0064/D-0069, D-0105/D-0109, D-0122, D-0173, D-0286 and D-0132/D-0137. This completes the adapters, CI contract, commands and documentation for the request.

usage.summary: Wrote [issues.json](/var/folders/fz/s3p17rl97r30y73d180fjbmc0000gn/T/invariant-plan-3742873294/issues.json) with six ordered issues covering modeled prerequisites, adapters, watcher integration and documentation. The plan check passed on its first run; `repo/` remains unchanged.
